text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic receives Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Igor Ivanov. Two sides agree that internal problems of a country should be resolved within its legal institutions.

- Serbian government appoints new general manager and board of directors of state power company EPS, blaming previous management for omissions in organisation and functioning of the company. It also appoints new manager of PTT Serbia.
- Visiting Deputy chairman of the Russian lower house of Parliament, Sergei Baburin, says Serbia's post-electoral crisis should not be linked to the Kosovo issue.

- Yugoslav Trade Union Federation supports all justified workers protests which call for necessary economic, social and democratic reforms and calls on state to finally take over social functions, says president Dragan Radulovic.
- Subotica company Braca Djordjevic and German firm Sinalco sign a five million dollar deal for production and sale of natural juices and non-alcoholic beverages.

- Serbian shipbuilding is the most promising branch of the economy. It increased its production by 90 percent and exports by 8.5 percent in 1996 in relation to the previous year and has concluded export deals worth $315 million for 1997.
- Serbian petrol industry NIS Jugopetrol subscribes 5.1 million German marks worth of shares of the daily Politika.
- Serbian government says 1.5 million hectares will be sown with wheat this spring.

- Serbian government is elected by majority of deputies in republican parliament in which deputies of ruling Socialist party of Serbia, New Democracy, and 1. Decembra have necessary majority, writes paper ahead of government reshuffle.
- Workers of department stores Company Beograd end six-week strike following general manager's resignation.
NASA BORBA
- Neither oppoosition nor authorities in Serbia wish OSCE to mediate in the problems created following annulment of local election results.
- Opposition leaders describe Serbia's protesters as champions of pacifism as protest rallies and marches continue.

- Serbian teachers on strike. Out of 515 secondary schools in Serbia only 41 on strike, according to assistant education minister Vojislav Braunovic. Trade Union leader Jagos Bulatovic says increasing number of schools on strike, 124 in Belgrade alone.
- Independent trade union of City Transport company again announces strike because workers' demands have not been met.
- Serbian President Milosevic purchasing real estate in Greece, says Greek daily Eleftherotypia.
- Macedonian authorities blocked visit of Serbian Orthodox Church delegation on Saint Sava day.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Massacre in Pec courtroom where policeman Nikola Berisa, on trial for police abuses, kills two, injures one and flees.
- Financial situation of Yugoslav army more difficult than ever. The state is not settling its dues to the army regularly, says Colonel Radisa Djordjevic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Out of 276 schools in Belgrade 120 on strike despite Education ministry announcement that first part of December wages would be paid.
